_about: Rewrite of guide #287 (2026-10-22, write-article). Every number and rule in the new body traces to an entry here.
question: I'm buying a house that has (or may have) unpermitted work. What do I take on, and what do I do before closing?
verdictConfirmed: First check whether the work needed a permit at all; if it did, the problem passes to whoever owns and occupies the house, legalizing it costs an extra fee on top of the permit in the model code, the lender's appraiser comments on it rather than automatically rejecting it, and seller disclosure forms only ask what the seller is aware of -- so settle it (permit, credit or walk) before closing.

facts.claim: IRC 2021 R105.1: any owner or owner's authorized agent who intends to construct, enlarge, alter, repair, move, demolish or change the occupancy of a building, or install/alter electrical, gas, mechanical or plumbing systems regulated by the code, must first apply and obtain the required permit.
facts.quote: Any owner or owner's authorized agent who intends to construct, enlarge, alter, repair, move, demolish or change the occupancy of a building or structure ... shall first make application to the building official and obtain the required permit.

facts.claim: IRC 2021 R105.2 work exempt from permit (building): one-story detached accessory structures up to 200 square feet (not storm shelters); fences not over 7 feet; retaining walls not over 4 feet unless supporting a surcharge; sidewalks and driveways; painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, counter tops and similar finish work; prefabricated pools under 24 inches deep; swings and playground equipment; window awnings projecting no more than 54 inches; decks not exceeding 200 square feet, not more than 30 inches above grade at any point, not attached to the dwelling and not serving the required exit door (R311.4). Plumbing: stopping leaks and clearing stoppages, unless concealed pipe must be removed and replaced, which is new work needing a permit. The exemption does not authorize work that violates the code or other local laws or ordinances.
facts.quote: Exemption from permit requirements of this code shall not be deemed to grant authorization for any work to be done in any manner in violation of the provisions of this code or any other laws or ordinances of this jurisdiction. ... 1. ... one-story detached accessory structures, provided that the floor area does not exceed 200 square feet ... 2. Fences not over 7 feet ... 3. Retaining walls that are not over 4 feet ... 5. Sidewalks and driveways. 6. Painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, counter tops and similar finish work. ... 10. Decks not exceeding 200 square feet ... not more than 30 inches ... above grade at any point, are not attached to a dwelling and do not serve the exit door required by Section R311.4. ... Plumbing: 1. The stopping of leaks ... if any concealed trap, drainpipe ... becomes defective and it becomes necessary to remove and replace the same with new material, such work shall be considered as new work and a permit shall be obtained

facts.claim: IRC 2021 R108.6: anyone who starts work requiring a permit before obtaining it is subject to a fee set by the governing authority in addition to the required permit fees.
facts.quote: Any person who commences work requiring a permit ... before obtaining the necessary permits shall be subject to a fee established by the applicable governing authority that shall be in addition to the required permit fees.

facts.claim: IRC 2021 R113.1 makes it unlawful to erect, alter ... or OCCUPY a building in violation of the code; R113.2 lets the building official serve a notice of violation on the person responsible for the construction, alteration ... or occupancy, directing abatement of the violation.
facts.quote: It shall be unlawful for any person, firm or corporation to erect, construct, alter, extend, repair, move, remove, demolish or occupy any building ... in conflict with or in violation of any of the provisions of this code. ... The building official is authorized to serve a notice of violation or order on the person responsible for the erection, construction, alteration, extension, repair, moving, removal, demolition or occupancy of a building ... Such order shall direct the discontinuance of the illegal action or condition and the abatement of the violation.

facts.claim: IRC 2021 R105.5: a permit becomes invalid if work isn't started within 180 days of issuance or if more than 180 days pass between inspections; the building official may grant written extensions of up to 180 days each.
facts.quote: Every permit issued shall become invalid unless the work authorized by such permit is commenced within 180 days after its issuance or after commencement of work if more than 180 days pass between inspections.

facts.claim: Fannie Mae Selling Guide B4-1.3-05 (dated 06/04/2025), 'Additions without Permits': if the appraiser identifies an addition without the required permit, the appraiser must comment on the quality and appearance of the work and its impact, if any, on market value.
facts.quote: If the appraiser identifies an addition(s) that does not have the required permit, the appraiser must comment on the quality and appearance of the work and its impact, if any, on the market value of the subject property.

facts.claim: Texas Property Code 5.008: the statutory seller's disclosure notice item 9 asks whether the seller is aware of room additions, structural modifications, or other alterations or repairs made without necessary permits or not in compliance with building codes in effect at that time. 5.008(e): the section does not apply to transfers including court order or foreclosure sale, by a fiduciary administering a decedent's estate, guardianship, conservatorship or trust, between co-owners, to a spouse or lineal relative, a never-occupied new residence of not more than one dwelling unit, among others (11 categories). 5.008(f): if a contract is entered without the notice, the purchaser may terminate for any reason within seven days after receiving the notice.
facts.quote: 9. Are you (Seller) aware of any of the following? ... Room additions, structural modifications, or other alterations or repairs made without necessary permits or not in compliance with building codes in effect at that time. ... (e) This section does not apply to a transfer: (1) pursuant to a court order or foreclosure sale; ... (5) by a fiduciary in the course of the administration of a decedent's estate ... (10) of a new residence of not more than one dwelling unit which has not previously been occupied ... (f) ... the purchaser may terminate the contract for any reason within seven days after receiving the notice.

facts.claim: Washington RCW 64.06.020 seller disclosure statement (version effective until January 1, 2027, and the 2027 version): asks whether there have been conversions, additions or remodeling, and if yes whether all building permits were obtained and whether all final inspections were obtained, each with a Don't know option. RCW 64.06.010: the chapter does not apply to foreclosures or deeds in lieu, transfers by an estate's personal representative or a bankruptcy trustee, certain family transfers, or where the buyer expressly waived the statement. RCW 64.06.030: within three business days of receiving the statement (or as otherwise agreed) the buyer may approve it or rescind the agreement, with deposits returned.
facts.quote: Have there been any conversions, additions, or remodeling? [ ] Yes [ ] No [ ] Don't know (1) If yes, were all building permits obtained? ... (2) If yes, were all final inspections obtained? ... This chapter does not apply to ... (1) A foreclosure or deed-in-lieu of foreclosure; ... (6) A transfer made by the personal representative of the estate of the decedent or by a trustee in bankruptcy; and (7) A transfer in which the buyer has expressly waived the receipt of the seller disclosure statement. ... Within three business days, or as otherwise agreed to, of receipt of the real property transfer disclosure statement, the buyer shall have the right to ... (2) rescinding the agreement
